designNotes:
Editorial review layout built on the existing slate and orange palette, using only local system fonts. A sticky bar holds the unchanged dashboard mark and links to the six scenes and to the notes. Each link gets an orange dot once a note is written there. The cover states the status first: proposed interfaces, fictional sample data, nothing built, and notes are not authorization. Next come a contents grid, the terminal → plan → work → evidence → review path, the five separate facts (worker completion, evidence, result submission, origin acceptance, merge) and the ten current views. Each scene opens with a large number and title. The image then runs wider than the text column, with a 'Proposed interface · fictional sample data' bar above it, then the caption. Below that, Keeps, Adds or extends and Limits sit beside the review-question card. The enlarge dialog (native <dialog>) offers Fit, 100%, 150% and 200% zoom, plus Previous and Next, click-to-zoom at a point, drag-to-pan, keyboard + / − / 0, and Escape to close. It repeats the concept label, and the full image always stays scrollable. Notes save to a draft in localStorage under 'agentmux.visual-review.2026-10-09.notes.v1'. If the browser blocks saving, the page says so and warns before you leave. Download builds a Markdown file from a Blob. If the download is blocked, the notes appear as copyable text. A CSP meta tag (default-src 'none') blocks every network load. Without JS, all content and text boxes still work; the enlarge and save controls stay hidden and a notice explains this. Print uses black on white, hides controls and prints each note as text.

Integration notes for Codex:
- Replace every {{LOGO_DATA_URI}} (there are three) with a base64 data:image/svg+xml URI.
- {{PLAN_DATA_URI}} is a data:text/markdown;charset=utf-8;base64 URI.
- Fill {{SCENES}} with the six renderScene outputs, joined in ID order.
- Use function replacements (or split/join) so '$' sequences in the data are not interpreted.
- Pass phase as the phase list only, for example 'P05–P07' or 'P08 and P10'. The renderer adds the 'Plan phases' prefix.
- sceneCss uses the :root tokens and the .vh class from the page CSS. The dialog reuses .concept-tag from sceneCss.
- renderScene keeps the existing test contract: escaped alt, the -title and -note IDs, the concept label, and rejection of remote images and unsafe IDs. It also validates the two-digit number and that every text prop is a non-empty string.
